cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: The WAL is the storage engine's physical redo log: every change to data pages is written there first, so after a crash committed transactions can be replayed. The binlog is MySQL's server-level logical log of row changes or statements, used for replication and point-in-time recovery.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: WAL is physical (page offsets), compact and fast; binlog is logical, written at commit. In MySQL they are kept consistent by an internal two-phase commit: InnoDB writes a prepare to the redo log, then the binlog, then commits. PostgreSQL has no separate binlog; its WAL does both jobs.

questions.q: MySQL crashes after the WAL write but before the binlog. Is the transaction committed?
questions.a: No. Internal two-phase commit rolls it back because it was only prepared.

questions.q: Which log is for crash recovery?
Which log does MySQL use for replication?
